report.summary: Reviewed chunk 1 of subprocess_adapter.py: dataclasses, profiles, session creation, publishing, send. Claims mostly kept, a few uncheckable.
risks: create_session | medium | prompt_mode 'argument' with empty prompt silently drops prompt; docstring implies prompt always sent; test would clarify expected behavior.
create_session | medium | stdin_prompt_marker appended even when prompt is empty; codex gets '-' with no prompt; test would clarify intended behavior.
create_session | low | prompt_mode 'none' with empty prompt is allowed; docstring says profile does not accept a prompt, but empty prompt passes; test would confirm intent.
_publish | medium | metadata uses self._sessions[session_id] without checking existence; a race or bad session id raises KeyError; test would exercise missing session.
create_session | low | stderr_task reads entire stderr into memory unbounded; large output could exhaust memory; test with large stderr would settle.
create_session | low | session_id uses command stem which may not be unique across different runtimes; uuid suffix reduces collision; test with same stem different runtimes.

handoff.purpose: Define RuntimeConfig, runtime profiles, _Session, SubprocessAdapter constructor, factory methods, capabilities, create_session, stdin writing, send, and event publish.

symbols.name: RuntimeConfig
symbols.note: Frozen dataclass holding verified process-launch contract: command, args, streaming, resume, hidden state, output format, prompt mode, markers, args, env, timeout.

symbols.name: RUNTIME_PROFILES
symbols.note: dict[str, RuntimeConfig] with 'claude' and 'codex' profiles; comment says one-shot, non-interactive invocations.

symbols.name: _Session
symbols.note: Dataclass holding process, cwd, stderr_task, started_at, timeout_s.

symbols.name: SubprocessAdapter
symbols.note: AgentAdapter subclass; runs configured CLI in bounded working directory; normalizes output.

symbols.name: __init__
symbols.note: Constructor; accepts config or command; validates repo_root; initializes sessions, sink, runtime_name, sequences.

symbols.name: from_name
symbols.note: Classmethod factory from profile name; raises ValueError for unknown name.

symbols.name: capabilities
symbols.note: Returns AgentCapabilities with streaming from config, resume from config, hidden_state_access False.

symbols.name: create_session
symbols.note: Spawns subprocess, stores session, writes prompt to stdin if prompt_mode is stdin, publishes input message.

symbols.name: _write_stdin
symbols.note: Writes text plus newline to process stdin; raises if session missing or stdin closed.

symbols.name: send
symbols.note: Publishes user message and writes text to stdin.

symbols.name: _publish
symbols.note: Publishes transport record via sink with sequence and metadata; no-op if sink is None.

claims.text: This is a process/event normalization layer, not a universal agent protocol: each CLI still needs a verified command profile and provider-specific event parser.
claims.why: The chunk defines profiles and adapter but does not show event parsing or verification; reaches beyond this chunk.

claims.text: Built-in profiles are limited to CLIs whose local --help contract is exercised by tests and whose execution is one-shot.
claims.why: No tests or --help verification in this chunk; profiles are one-shot in design but no evidence of tests.

claims.text: Antigravity isn't listed: no agy executable or stable JSON protocol exists on this machine, and a desktop/IDE session does not imply a callable CLI contract.
claims.why: The absence of 'agy' is observable in this chunk, but the reason (no executable, no protocol) is external; cannot verify machine state.

claims.text: These profiles describe one-shot, non-interactive invocations.
claims.why: Profiles use --print, --verbose, --input-format text, --output-format stream-json, --permission-mode dontAsk for claude; codex uses exec --json --ask-for-approval never --sandbox workspace-write; these are one-shot, non-interactive.

claims.text: Run a configured CLI in a bounded working directory and normalize output.
claims.why: Bounded working directory is implemented (cwd resolution, session cwd), but output normalization is in chunk 2 (events parsing).

claims.text: Either config or command must be provided
claims.why: If config is None and command falsy, raises ValueError with message 'Either config or command must be provided'.
If root.is_dir() is False, raises ValueError with that message.

claims.text: Unknown or unverified runtime ... Pass an explicit RuntimeConfig for a custom CLI.
claims.why: If profile is None, raises ValueError with message including 'Unknown or unverified runtime' and 'Pass an explicit RuntimeConfig for a custom CLI.'

claims.text: session cwd is not a directory
claims.why: If resolved cwd is not a directory, raises ValueError with that message.
If timeout_s <= 0, raises ValueError with that message.
If model given and model_arg is None, raises ValueError with message containing 'profile has no model option'.

claims.text: profile does not accept a prompt
claims.why: If prompt_mode is 'none' and prompt is truthy, raises ValueError with message containing 'profile does not accept a prompt'.

claims.text: session {session_id} not found or stdin unavailable
claims.why: If session is None or process.stdin is None, raises RuntimeError with that message.
If process.stdin.is_closing() is True, raises RuntimeError with that message.

observations.what: create_session: when prompt_mode is 'argument' and prompt is empty, the prompt is neither appended to cmd nor published; the input message is not sent.
When prompt_mode is 'stdin' and stdin_prompt_marker is set, the marker is appended even when prompt is empty; codex gets '-' with no prompt.
When prompt_mode is 'none' and prompt is empty, no error is raised; the docstring says the profile does not accept a prompt, but empty prompt is allowed.
_publish uses self._sessions[session_id] without checking existence; a missing session id raises KeyError.
stderr_task reads entire stderr into memory; large stderr could exhaust memory.
session_id uses command stem, which may be shared across different runtimes; uuid suffix reduces but does not eliminate collision risk.
